metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills 2023 – Country Notes: Korea

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The Survey of Adult Skills 2023 uses a household survey design with a sample drawn to be representative of the adult population (ages 16–65) in Korea, irrespective of nationality/citizenship/language status. The country notes report response rate and describe non-response bias checks, but they do not provide the specific weight variable names (e.g., final sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures. For OECD/PIAAC-style adult skills reporting, analysts typically apply the provided survey weights when estimating population-representative means and proficiency distributions, and use the associated uncertainty estimation approach (e.g., confidence intervals) consistent with the complex design. Because this country note does not document the exact weight variables or replicate method, the weighting strategy is described at the design level rather than operationalized with explicit weight codes.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country note that reports descriptive proficiency results (means on 500-point scales, proficiency levels, and shares at levels) and relationships with outcomes, rather than fitting an ML model with an explicitly stated PV-based achievement outcome. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of not being an ML/PV estimation pipeline described in this note. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note focuses on published estimates and does not document the imputation/deletion rules used in the underlying OECD production process.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Korea 2022–23 Survey of Adult Skills sample (adults aged 16–65) with a household survey design. The note indicates that doorstep interviews were offered to respondents not sufficiently fluent in the assessment language, and that doorstep respondents are generally excluded when comparing across cycles to maximise comparability; however, the note does not specify whether the reported proficiency and outcome comparisons for Korea include or exclude doorstep-only respondents beyond the general exclusion statement.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarises results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Korea, using adults aged 16–65 assessed in three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. The assessment is administered exclusively on digital tablets and proficiency is reported on 500-point scales with proficiency levels derived from task success/failure and item difficulty. For Korea, mean performance is below the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 249, numeracy 253, adaptive problem solving 238). The note reports the distribution across proficiency levels (e.g., literacy: 31% at Level 1 or below; numeracy: 28% at or below Level 1; adaptive problem solving: 37% at or below Level 1) and highlights age differences (older adults 55–65 score lower than 25–34). It also describes trends versus the 2011–12 cycle (declines in literacy and numeracy and widening gaps) and associations between higher skills and better employment, well-being, and civic outcomes, while noting that doorstep respondents are generally excluded for cross-cycle comparability.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD country note rather than an empirical ML paper: it does not specify a predictive modeling pipeline, target variables for ML, or algorithmic evaluation metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, PV handling in an ML context, and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty. The note also does not provide the underlying production-method details (e.g., PV estimation and missing-data procedures), which are typically documented in OECD technical documentation rather than in country notes.
